claims.hypothesis: The wide dust gap (~70 au) in the protoplanetary disk around [BHB2007]-1 is carved by a planet or brown dwarf companion.
claims.experiment: Analyzed VLT/NACO high-contrast NIR images (J, H, K_S, L') after stellar PSF subtraction and compared with ALMA continuum/CO and VLA 14-mm maps.
claims.result: Detected a point-like source in L' band at 53 au (0.32'', PA 186 deg) inside the ALMA mm gap, spatially coincident with a VLA 14-mm source, with an L' flux ratio of 1.4e-2 corresponding to 37-47 M_Jup.
claims.finding: A candidate substellar companion of 37-47 M_Jup is located inside the disk cavity, compatible with the mass required to open the ALMA cavity and filter micron-sized dust grains down to <20 au.

evidence.quote: This object is constrained to have a mass in the range of 37-47 M$_{Jup}$ and is located at 50 au from the central star, inside the 70 au-large disk cavity recently imaged by ALMA
The candidate companion is located at a distance of 53 au (0.32$''$), at a position angle of 186$\degree$.
Comparing our numbers with the modeling by (cite: Villenave2019) reveals that a sub-stellar object ($M>13 {\rm M_{jup}}$) is needed to account for the observed discrepancy.

claims.hypothesis: The strong brightness asymmetry between the southern and northern sides of the NIR scattered-light disk is caused by a shadow cast by a misaligned inner disk.
claims.experiment: Measured the disk-to-stellar light contrast on the northern and southern sides of the disk across J, H, K_S, and L' wavebands.
claims.result: The disk brightness decreases with wavelength from 17.2% to 6.0% on the bright south side, while the South-to-North brightness ratio remains constant across all four bands at an average of 5.6.
claims.finding: The wavelength-independent brightness ratio indicates differential illumination due to shadowing of the northern disk side by a misaligned inner disk or warp potentially induced by the massive companion.

evidence.quote: The constant amount of asymmetry across all wavelengths suggests that it is due to a shadow cast by a misaligned inner disk.
Nonetheless, the brightness ratio between the southern and northern sides is constant (with an average ratio of 5.6).
The constancy of the brightness ratio across wavelengths (see Table 2) suggests that the difference is due to a different amount of illumination.

claims.hypothesis: The discrepancy between the photometric stellar mass (0.65-0.85 M_sun) and the ALMA CO dynamical mass (2.23 M_sun) of [BHB2007]-1 can be explained by an unresolved equal-mass central binary.
claims.experiment: Derived stellar luminosity and mass from B-to-W4 photometry, Phoenix photosphere models, and pre-main-sequence evolutionary tracks, and compared against the CO dynamical mass.
claims.result: Photometric stellar mass is 0.65-0.85 M_sun for T_eff = 4060 K; evolutionary tracks at 4000 K are nearly vertical, and reconciling with the dynamical mass via temperature alone would require T_eff > 5000 K.
claims.finding: Errors in luminosity or T_eff alone cannot explain the mass discrepancy, suggesting the central star could speculatively be an unresolved nearly equal-mass binary.

evidence.quote: The stellar mass of [BHB2007]-1 is significantly smaller than what was constrained by (cite: Alves2020) from the position-velocity diagram of the CO emission (2.23 $\rm M_{\odot}$).
A possible, and yet speculative, solution could be that the central star is in reality an unresolved binary with nearly equal-mass components (cite: Andersen1989; Czekala2015).

why_this_data.value: VLT/NACO high-contrast NIR imaging in J, H, K_S, and L' probes scattered light from micron-sized dust and thermal emission from embedded companions inside the millimeter gap.

evidence.quote: We present VLT/NACO high-contrast images in $J$, $H$, $K_S$, and $L^{\prime}$ band of the young star [BHB2007]-1 probing the inclined disk in scattered light and revealing the probable presence of a companion.
The $L^\prime$ image, which traces thermal emission as well as scattered light signal, shows a bright peak close to the gap, in the south side of the disk.

why_this_method.value: Reconstructing the stellar PSF via an azimuthal average over emission-free angles produced qualitatively better subtraction than using a 2D Gaussian or a scaled field star PSF, and removed Airy rings in L'.

evidence.quote: This procedure produced qualitatively better results than subtracting an 2D Gaussian or a scaled version of the PSF given by another star in the field. In $L^\prime$ band, the PSF subtraction allows to remove the Airy rings.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Subtracting a 2D Gaussian or a scaled PSF of another star in the field (rejected in favor of azimuthally averaged radial PSF profile).

evidence.quote: This procedure produced qualitatively better results than subtracting an 2D Gaussian or a scaled version of the PSF given by another star in the field.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Gaia EDR3 parallax distance of 232.6 pc for [BHB2007]-1 (rejected as spurious due to low astrometric fidelity of 0.05053, large astrometric excess noise, CO systemic velocity matching Barnard 59, and unphysically large implied disk size).

evidence.quote: The astrometric fidelities are 0.9995 and 0.05053 for BHB2007-2 and BHB2007-1, respectively, meaning that the astrometric solution of the latter source is most likely spurious.
Therefore, we are inclined to consider the Gaia EDR3 parallax erroneous and assume a distance of 166 pc, like [BHB2007]-2.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Erroneous stellar luminosity or effective temperature as the cause of the discrepancy between photometric and dynamical stellar mass (rejected because PMS tracks at 4000 K are nearly vertical and T_eff > 5000 K is implausible given NIR spectra).

evidence.quote: Such a large discrepancy cannot be explained by an erroneous estimate of the stellar luminosity alone since the evolutionary tracks in correspondence of stars with $T_{\rm eff}=4000$ K are nearly vertical
A miscalculation of the effective temperature is also an unlikely explanation. In fact, a $T_{\rm eff}>5000$ K would be necessary to reconcile photometric and dynamical mass.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: L' emission arising from a circumplanetary disk of a forming protoplanet rather than photospheric emission of a brown dwarf.

evidence.quote: It is also possible that the $L^\prime$ emission comes from a circumplanetary disk of a still forming protoplanet.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Gravitational influence from the neighboring binary [BHB2007]-2 causing the disk brightness asymmetry.

evidence.quote: An alternative scenario is that the difference in the luminosity is caused by the presence of the binary system [BHB2007]-2.

limitations_admitted.value: Poor quality of the first-epoch NB_1.64 observation prevents detecting any potential jet emission and causes large astrometric errorbars for [BHB2007]-2B.

evidence.quote: However, the bad quality of our NACO observations does not allow to detect any emission from the potential jet.
It is then difficult to infer any orbital motion between [BHB2007]-2 A and B, due to the great errorbars.

limitations_admitted.value: Edge-on disk geometry may cause an underestimation of the stellar luminosity of [BHB2007]-1.

evidence.quote: However, the edge-on geometry of the disk (see Sect. 3.4) may in principle yield an under-estimation of the luminosity.

limitations_admitted.value: Residual scattered light from the circumstellar disk may remain at the companion location after PSF subtraction, making the derived companion mass (37-47 M_Jup) an upper limit.

evidence.quote: Although, some residual light from the circumstellar disk may still be present at the location of the PSF, and the following assumption for its mass is then the upper limit, as its brightness can be overestimated.

limitations_admitted.value: The measured companion distance (50-53 au) is only the projected separation on the sky rather than the true semi-major axis, and follow-up observations are required to confirm whether the companion is bound.

evidence.quote: The nature of this detection can only be confirmed with a follow-up measurement.
A caveat is that the current distance of the companion may not be the semi-major axis, as what we measure is the projected separation on the sky.

referee_caveats_inferred: The candidate companion is only detected in a single NIR band (L') at a single epoch inside a bright, highly inclined scattered-light disk, so confusion with a disk feature or residual PSF structure cannot be fully ruled out without multi-epoch common proper motion confirmation.
A large unresolved discrepancy exists between the photometric stellar mass (0.65-0.85 M_sun) and the ALMA CO dynamical mass (2.23 M_sun).
